patch_resolves_note: The official patch.diff resets cleanly only for source hunks; its added regression font is a binary patch that does not apply in the staged workspace. Stage 04 therefore used a one-line source-equivalent fix patch for `src/silf.cc` to collect the fixed assertion trace, and separately confirmed the authoritative `n132/arvo:30983-fix` image runs the staged PoC cleanly. Both witnesses agree on the real mechanism change: `new uint8_t[decompressed_size]` becomes `new uint8_t[decompressed_size]()` before recursive SILF reparse.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

nodes.description: First project-side materialization of the attacker-controlled SILF table bytes and their extent into parser state.

Missing initialization obligation: the LZ4 destination buffer is heap-allocated without zero-initialization even though the parser later trusts the full declared decompressed span after only a returned-length check.
MemorySanitizer crash site. `ReadU16` consumes two bytes from the recursive SILF buffer and byte-swaps them as a 16-bit value while `SILPass::ParsePart` is reading a `stateTrans` cell.
Intermediate runtime event reparse_call materialized from verified transition assertion A-ALLOC-TO-REPARSE.

edges.evidence: The vulnerable original records `decompress_alloc.decompressed_ptr == reparse_call.parse_data == 0x745453818000`, and the fixed witness records the same equality at its own heap address.
The vulnerable original records `reparse_call.parse_data == readu16_sink.buffer_base == 0x745453818000`, showing the same decompressed heap buffer reaches Buffer::ReadU16 unchanged.
